## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Meṇḍakapañhajātaka* (Ja 471) is a narrative within the canonical Pāli Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional editorial framework, the problem or tale of Meṇḍaka is cross-referenced or given fully under the Ummagga Birth (*Mahā-ummagga Jātaka*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records translations of the text in four modern languages [SuttaCentral].

Epigraphic and artistic evidence from the Pagan period in Burma demonstrates that the story was regularly identified and depicted in temple illustrations [WinThanTun 2002]. In Pagan-era temple plaques and inscriptions, the Jātaka appears under several variant titles and spellings, including *Mendakapañha* (found at Winido and Shwezigon), *Mendapañha* (at Ajagona, Chaukhpayahla, and Gubyaukgyi [Myinkaba]), *Mindapañha* (at Thingaraza and Thambula), *Mendoka* (at Gubyaukgyi [Wetkyi-in]), and *Siriminda* (at the Ananda Temple) [WinThanTun 2002].
